Transpose

tranz-POHZ · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To transpose to transfer to a different place; to switch the order of two things.

The choir director asked the pianist to transpose the hymn down a full step so more voices could reach the low notes.

Worked Example

To make the song easier to sing, the choir director transposed the entire piece up two keys before rehearsal.

Shifting something -- notes, digits, letters -- into a different position or order is exactly what transpose describes.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — trans-

prefix — trans-: across (Latin)

root — -pose (ponere)

root — -pose (ponere): to place (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Transpose comes from Latin trans- ('across') plus ponere ('to place') -- literally 'to place across' or 'to place in a different order.' To transpose two things is to switch their places or order.
